items.title: Marty Sheller interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 9, 2022
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Yes. I know what you’re saying and I remember Bela Fleck, the wonderful banjo player said that he just kept a list of titles.

ctx.x: Good question. I never think of a title before I start to write. I know certain composers will get an idea about I don’t know, look out the window and see a beautiful scene and say that reminds me of the time I went to Acapulco so I’m going to write something that would be appropriate for that. I’m the opposite. I write strictly by the notes and the chords and the harmonies. And when I get to the end I say now what am I going to call this? And it’s the truth. I’m terrible with that. I mean I can’t even remember…

Yes. I know what you’re saying and I remember Bela Fleck, the wonderful banjo player said that he just kept a list of titles. He’d see a word, “Well that could be a song,” and next time he needed one he’d look at the list.
There you go. I can understand that. © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-
